title: Modernize batch execution graph and shrink KV metadata footprint
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation:
We have accumulated complexity across the continuous batch execution graph and the on-disk/in-memory KV metadata layer. This manifests as high GC churn in the KV index, brittle scheduler heuristics, and a long tail for short requests. This ticket consolidates a focused refactor to: 1) convert the execution graph to a pipelined model with explicit lightweight handoffs, 2) compress per-session KV metadata and epoch markers, and 3) simplify scheduler fast paths to reduce contention.

Scope:
- Replace the ad-hoc chained futures in the batch graph with a compact pipeline stage abstraction (Stage, TokenBatch, Handshake) to reduce intermediate allocations.
- Introduce a compact epoch marker for KV metadata (packed 64-bit headers) to remove per-entry maps used only for liveness checks.
- Move hot liveness checks off the global epoch lock and into a read-optimized tombstone bitmap per-shard.
- Simplify scheduler admission fast-path: single-slot optimistic commit, with a clear fallback path that avoids global coordination for common cases.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Memory layout: choose packed struct over small objects to reduce pointer chasing at the cost of a one-time migration on shard restart. Migration will be lazy and backwards-compatible.
- Handshake model: optimistic single-slot commit assumes most sessions finish quickly; this greatly reduces contention but will add a bounded retry window for long-running sessions.
- KV tombstone bitmap uses extra shard-local memory (~0.5% per-shard) to avoid global locks; measured trade-off favors latency improvements.

Progress so far:
- Spike completed: prototype pipeline stage API and benchmark harness (bench results attached).
- KV metadata packing design reviewed with storage team (notes linked).
- Scheduler fast-path sketch implemented behind feature flag.
- Performance tests on a dev cluster: median tail R99 reduced by 18% on conversational microbenchmarks; token throughput unchanged.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: interop with legacy KV snapshotting. Mitigation: keep dual readers for one release cycle and add migration toggle in shard startup.
- Risk: regressions for long-lived sessions due to optimistic commit. Mitigation: add telemetry and kill-switch; run canary traffic for 48h before enabling globally.

Next steps / checklist:
- [ ] Finish migration shim for restoring legacy snapshots (owner: @Priya).
- [ ] Add comprehensive unit tests for packed epoch headers and tombstone bitmap.
- [ ] Wire-up telemetry for handshake retries and prometheus metrics for tombstone hits.
- [ ] Run canary on dedicated-qa cluster using production-like traffic template.
- [ ] Coordinate with ops for controlled rollout and rollback playbook.

Related artifacts and context:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Batch+Pipeline+and+KV+Metadata+Compression
- Spike benchmark repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-spikes/pull/88
- Feature branch PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2074
- Perf dashboard (dev cluster): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/3a2b4/pipeline-kv-refactor
- Incident notes referencing tail problems: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2024-11-kv-tail-latency-notes

Review feedback (summary):
- Storage team: OK with packed header format if migration is lazy. Asked to add checksum to header for future compatibility.
- Scheduler lead: prefer conservative defaults for optimistic commit retries. Suggested telemetry names and thresholds.
- QA: request additional fuzz tests for interleaved commit/eviction sequences.

Follow-up tasks (will create sub-issues):
- Lightweight migration CL that can run during shard restart windows (ENG-469272).
- Add extended integration test that simulates hotkey churn with tombstone bitmap (ENG-469273).
acceptance_criteria: R99 tail latency for short sessions decreases by >=15% on synthetic conversational workload compared to baseline
KV metadata memory usage per-shard reduced by at least 20% on average in our dev cluster
Feature gated; canary rollout completed for 48h with no increase in error rate or latency for production-like traffic
Telemetry exposes handshake retry rate, tombstone bitmap hit rate, and migration failures
Backward-compatible snapshot restore verified in integration tests
notes: Bench summary (dev cluster): median latency 10ms -> 8.2ms, R99 120ms -> 98ms. Memory per-shard from ~82MB -> ~64MB for metadata. Initial canary plan scheduled for 2025-02-25. Code review requested from @storage-team and @scheduler-team.
